historical_reviews.v3_1: Surprise-add acceptance begins before insertion: the OS must reach a stable, expected topology with the target serial and BDF absent. The live insertion must then produce one ordered PCIe/NVMe add sequence, bind the returning serial to the intended bay/BDF, establish expected namespaces and link width, and leave no AER, timeout or BMC discrepancy.

original_test_intent: Validate supported live surprise addition of an E1.S drive after the system boots with that drive physically absent, across OS, BMC/IPMI and PCIe surfaces.
original_method: Map and quiesce the selected drive, capture its present baseline, cleanly shut down and have an operator remove it, boot to a stable OS-with-empty-bay state and prove absence, then have the operator insert the same serial into the approved live-service bay while the Agent records complete PCIe/NVMe/BMC events and verifies link, namespace and health stabilization.
manual_activity: A storage/platform owner approves the exact surprise-add path; an authorized operator removes the drive while safely powered off and later inserts that same drive into the running hot-add-capable bay.
required_inputs: Vendor surprise-add procedure and supported bay
Approved shutdown and off-state removal steps
Expected PCIe/NVMe/BMC add events and deadlines
safety_requirements: Remove the selected drive only after approved shutdown/isolation
Prove it has no mounted, swap, RAID, LVM, mapper or workload dependencies
Insert only into a vendor-approved live-service bay
Verify the serial and bay before contact
Do not force discovery with rescan/reset
Stop on electrical, AER, kernel, I/O, link or BMC error
Do not retry a failed add
Do not change namespaces or format media
Preserve all boot and add logs
agent_execution_scope: Verify target map and quiesced state
Capture present baseline and shutdown evidence
Verify stable OS topology with the drive absent
Continuously collect kernel/PCIe/NVMe/BMC evidence during operator insertion
Bind returned serial and namespaces to the intended BDF and bay
Verify negotiated link and health stabilization
Archive evidence without physical action or verdict
engineer_actions: Approve bay capability and three-phase procedure
Supervise off-state removal and live insertion
Stop and direct recovery after any add anomaly
Resolve missing BMC or degraded-link evidence

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Enumeration plus `dmesg -T` covers part of the add observation, but omits the source-required off-state removal, stable boot-without-drive proof, BMC Web/IPMI state, per-BDF speed/bandwidth and exact same-drive recovery.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use complete read-only storage, PCIe, kernel and BMC collectors before removal, after boot without the drive, and continuously through one operator-controlled live insertion; do not automate hardware handling or force a rescan.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The shutdown/remove/boot/live-add sequence, source observation surfaces, private Script reference and 50-minute duration remain in scope.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Capture present-drive state, stable empty-bay boot state and same-serial live-add state as separate checkpoints joined by synchronized physical, kernel, PCIe, NVMe and BMC evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines measurable normality, identity and error-free stabilization while preserving the unique powered-off-removal/live-add sequence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A final `nvme list` can pass after an unrecorded rescan, wrong-drive insertion or degraded link and cannot prove the platform booted correctly with the bay empty.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Live insertion can cause electrical or PCIe errors and is human-only; successful enumeration does not by itself prove stable media or filesystem suitability.

project_override_considerations: Approve the hot-add-capable bay, expected empty-slot BMC/PCIe representation, OS/kernel support, add-event ordering and timeout, link-training criteria and whether the private Script performs any state-changing discovery action.
expected_evidence: Approved surprise-add procedure, Script revision and SUT/OS/kernel/backplane identity
Drive serial/controller/namespace/BDF/bay map, no-consumer proof and operator timestamps
Complete present baseline and clean shutdown/off-state removal record
OS-with-empty-bay boot, absence, BMC and preserved boot-log evidence
Synchronized live insertion, kernel/AER, PCIe, NVMe, BMC/IPMI and physical evidence
Same-serial link/namespace/health stabilization, no-reset/no-retry audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and Procedure consistently define surprise-add by powered-off removal, boot without the drive and live insertion. The broad `normal` criterion is incomplete but does not contradict the operation.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The add sequence is identifiable and vendor capability, target map and operator support are concrete prerequisites, so this is REQUIRES rather than BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Preserves the asymmetric surprise-add sequence and makes the empty-bay baseline, same-serial identity, link training and error-free event path independently auditable.
independent_technical_reasoning: A surprise-add test is not equivalent to re-adding a controller that the current boot previously enumerated. Booting with the bay empty exercises firmware and OS resource allocation for an absent endpoint; only after that stable baseline does live insertion test downstream-port discovery. Therefore evidence must prove absence first and then a clean, spontaneous add without reset or rescan assistance.
